findings.problem: Choice card 5 (Psalm 139:4) comes right after choice card 4. No story card sets up verse 4. The setup ("David even talks about the words he says") is in the question itself.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: Story card 3 is just the bare verse quote ("David says, 'I praise You, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.'"). It has none of Papa Dorin's voice, and it mostly repeats the answer to card 2.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Choice card 5 (Psalm 139:16) comes right after choice card 4. No story card sets up verse 16. The setup about the LORD's eyes seeing David's unformed body is told inside the question.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: Fill in the blank "written in the LORD's ___" with book / stone / sky asks the baker to guess the psalm's wording. "Written in stone" fits the meaning (days fixed before they came to be) just as well as "book". Only someone who already knows the verse can pick it.

rule.text: In poetry, letters and prophecy, the rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Choice card 11 (Psalm 139:21-22) comes right after choice card 10. No story card sets it up. Verse 21 is quoted inside the question instead.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: Choice card 12 (Psalm 139:23) comes right after choice card 11. No story card sets up the turn in verse 23. The question tells the turn itself, so it reads like a 50/50 guess, and story card 13 retells it afterward.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: The question says David asks God to see if there is any offensive way in him, "and then" to lead him. The BSB just puts the two requests side by side ("See if there is any offensive way in me; lead me in the way everlasting."). "And then" adds an order the text doesn't give.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
